name: issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_arms_heat
description: Issue #827 / #843 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). On a hot-classified day a dawn dip below comfort_heat (65F vs 68F) arms heat on the first reading below the floor and commands heat at comfort_heat. There is no tolerated dawn dip: the original #827 premise (a sub-deadband dip on a hot day never escalates because the sun will correct it) was reversed by #843 and is gone under #1066. Renamed from issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_within_deadband_no_escalate, whose 'no escalate within deadband' claim is false.
source: Issue #827 Design #1 (original no-escalate premise), reversed by Issue #843 and Issue #1066 (nearest-edge arming; no deadband tolerance for a breach).
notes: Occupant impact: a 65F house at dawn (3F below the 68F floor) must be heated within the first reading. The old energy-saving bet that the day would warm the house meant coasting below comfort; the cost of the new rule is a few minutes of furnace time.

Design D rule exercised: indoor < floor -> heating immediately on any day type, ignoring the dwell lock. Hot-day classification (hvac_mode=cool, windows_recommended=false, as classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_HOT) does not make heat 'against grain' any more. Duplicate note: this scenario and issue_827_missing_forecast_fallback_escalates.json differ only by day type and the (now irrelevant) thermal_model block.
Assertion time bounds are the first breach reading (06:15).

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) the hot-day deadband (5F, comfort_deadband_hot_f) holds a 3F breach indefinitely under the #827 rule, and even under the #843 recency rule heat needs a 90 s sustain across two evaluations, so at 06:15 comfort_family=heating and last_hvac_mode=heat fail.

(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('Mild/warm/hot day, indoor falls below the floor -> heat armed on the first reading'; 'Hot/cold 5F default becomes 2F, their old extra tolerance is gone').

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the household wakes in a house below its comfort floor while the thermostat sits in cool for the 'hot' day, as in the live incidents behind #843 and #1066.

events.note: Hot-day classification at dawn (classifier derives hvac_mode=cool, windows_recommended false). Indoor 71F is inside the band, no breach.
Dawn dip: indoor 65F, 3F below comfort_heat(68). Floor breach: heat is armed on this very reading regardless of the hot-day classification.
Periodic re-evaluation with indoor 65F: below the floor, so heat is armed and commanded at comfort_heat(68).

assertions.reason: Baseline: hot day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the ceiling.
A dawn dip below the floor arms heat on the first reading, regardless of day type; no deadband tolerance remains.
The commanded mode is a real climate service call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A dawn dip below comfort_heat on a hot-classified day arms heat on the first reading below the floor.
verdict.observed_behavior: Indoor drops to 65F (3F below the 68F floor) at 06:15; the family switches to heating and heat is commanded at comfort_heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Below the floor always means heat, immediately, on every day type (docs/08 section 6f); the old forecast-based dawn-dip tolerance is retired.
